s2_shape.disturbance: shared-code merge contention and conflicting concurrent edits
s2_shape.attenuation_relation: Grit symbol claims/locks, queues, isolated worktrees, serialized merge and release
s2_shape.subsequent_behavior_change: blocked or queued work waits rather than proceeding through the contested symbol

blocking_reasons: scripts/README.md states that runs write timestamped result directories, while scripts/.gitignore excludes */results/, so the raw CSV/log corpus underlying the README summary tables is not committed at the reviewed revision

the synthetic raw-git arm deliberately inserts file-level headers that guarantee conflicts, while the Grit arm uses a separately shuffled/partitioned symbol assignment, so the published comparison is not materially matched with the S2 relation as the only varying factor

the throughput benchmark independently allocates symbols in raw-git and Grit arms and adds file-level header/import edits, so its summary cannot isolate the Grit coordination relation as the causal varying factor
the real-agent benchmark publishes only the Grit-coordinated execution path and no matched no-Grit control at the reviewed revision
Grit is not a canonical Index harness/system boundary, so even a stronger first-party result would not by itself create a canonical native S2 row
reopen_when: the project publishes immutable raw benchmark result artifacts tied to an exact Grit revision and benchmark configuration
a materially matched public comparison holds workload/edit assignment constant while varying the Grit coordination relation
a public real-agent campaign includes a recoverable matched no-Grit control and Grit treatment with immutable provenance
non_claim: This review does not say Grit lacks S2-like coordination capability. It says the public evidence at the pinned revision is insufficient for an admitted capability-depth observation or direct-family promotion under the current provenance and matched-comparison rules.
